# Databricks Brain

> An Obsidian knowledge graph that teaches Databricks from zero to expert, told as one story:
> pre-Databricks history (chapters 01-05), the Databricks platform (06-10), the three clouds and
> administration (11-14), migrating a business (15), plus a front door for business readers (00),
> learning paths by persona (80), and a glossary (90).

Agent instructions: AGENTS.md. Full typed graph: _meta/vault_index.json. Blueprint: _meta/manifest.yaml.
Depth: 101 beginner, 201 practitioner, 301 advanced, 401 expert.


## Hubs

- [Cloud Comparison - Azure vs AWS vs GCP](Cloud%20Comparison%20-%20Azure%20vs%20AWS%20vs%20GCP.md): The same Databricks concept side by side on all three clouds, covering identity, network, storage, keys, and billing.
- [Databricks Product Names and Renames](Databricks%20Product%20Names%20and%20Renames.md): Current product names, old names, and when they changed. Check here before trusting any name.
- [Open Source vs Databricks - Who Replaced What](Open%20Source%20vs%20Databricks%20-%20Who%20Replaced%20What.md): Each open-source tool next to the Databricks feature that does its job today.
- [Persona Map](Persona%20Map.md): Which notes each persona should read, generated from note frontmatter.
- [Timeline of Data Engineering](Timeline%20of%20Data%20Engineering.md): Every milestone from relational databases to agents, in one timeline that links into the story.
- [start_here](start_here.md): The home page. Pick a door by who you are, or read the whole story from chapter 00.

## Is Databricks for You?

- [Chapter 00 - Is Databricks for You](00_is_databricks_for_you/Chapter%2000%20-%20Is%20Databricks%20for%20You.md): The front door. Who uses Databricks, what it costs, when it fits a small business, and when it does not.
- [What Databricks Is in Plain English](00_is_databricks_for_you/What%20Databricks%20Is%20in%20Plain%20English.md) [101]: Databricks in one page, with no jargon, for someone who has never heard of it.
- [Who Uses Databricks - Roles](00_is_databricks_for_you/Who%20Uses%20Databricks%20-%20Roles.md) [101]: The eight job roles that log in to Databricks, what each one does there, and which tools they use.
- [Who Uses Databricks - Business Types](00_is_databricks_for_you/Who%20Uses%20Databricks%20-%20Business%20Types.md) [101]: Kinds of businesses, from e-commerce to clinics to factories, that get real value from Databricks, with example use cases.
- [Signs You Have Outgrown Spreadsheets](00_is_databricks_for_you/Signs%20You%20Have%20Outgrown%20Spreadsheets.md) [101]: The warning signs that a business needs a real data platform instead of Excel, Access, or one reporting tool.
- [When Databricks Is Not the Right Fit](00_is_databricks_for_you/When%20Databricks%20Is%20Not%20the%20Right%20Fit.md) [101]: An honest list of situations where a simpler or cheaper tool is the better choice.
- [Databricks vs Alternatives for Small Teams](00_is_databricks_for_you/Databricks%20vs%20Alternatives%20for%20Small%20Teams.md) [201]: How Databricks compares with Snowflake, BigQuery, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI alone, and plain Postgres for a small team.
- [How Databricks Pricing Works](00_is_databricks_for_you/How%20Databricks%20Pricing%20Works.md) [101]: DBUs, SKUs, serverless versus classic, committed use, and why there are usually two bills.
- [Estimating Costs for a Small Business](00_is_databricks_for_you/Estimating%20Costs%20for%20a%20Small%20Business.md) [201]: A worked, back-of-the-envelope monthly cost estimate for a small company's first workloads.
- [Databricks Free Edition and Trials](00_is_databricks_for_you/Databricks%20Free%20Edition%20and%20Trials.md) [101]: The free ways to try Databricks (Free Edition and the 14-day trial), what each one includes, and what it leaves out.
- [Choosing a Cloud for Databricks](00_is_databricks_for_you/Choosing%20a%20Cloud%20for%20Databricks.md) [101]: How to pick Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud, based mostly on what the business already uses.
- [Your First 30 Days on Databricks](00_is_databricks_for_you/Your%20First%2030%20Days%20on%20Databricks.md) [101]: A week-by-week plan from sign-up to the first trusted dashboard.
- [Building a Business Case](00_is_databricks_for_you/Building%20a%20Business%20Case.md) [201]: How to justify Databricks to a boss or a board, covering costs, savings, risks, and a proof of concept.

## Foundations

- [Chapter 01 - Foundations](01_foundations/Chapter%2001%20-%20Foundations.md): The words and ideas everything else is built on, such as data, tables, SQL, files, and the cloud.
- [What Is Data](01_foundations/What%20Is%20Data.md) [101]: Data as recorded facts, and why businesses keep it.
- [Structured vs Unstructured Data](01_foundations/Structured%20vs%20Unstructured%20Data.md) [101]: Tables versus documents, images, audio, and logs, and the semi-structured data in between.
- [Files and File Formats](01_foundations/Files%20and%20File%20Formats.md) [101]: What a file format is and why the choice of format decides how fast and cheap data is to use.
- [CSV and JSON](01_foundations/CSV%20and%20JSON.md) [101]: The two most common plain-text data formats and their limits at scale.
- [Spreadsheets](01_foundations/Spreadsheets.md) [101]: Why Excel runs the world, and where it breaks.
- [Relational Databases](01_foundations/Relational%20Databases.md) [101]: Tables with rules and relationships, managed by software like Postgres, MySQL, and SQL Server.
- [SQL](01_foundations/SQL.md) [101]: The language for asking databases questions, and why it is still the most important data skill.
- [Primary and Foreign Keys](01_foundations/Primary%20and%20Foreign%20Keys.md) [101]: How rows get IDs and how tables point at each other.
- [OLTP vs OLAP](01_foundations/OLTP%20vs%20OLAP.md) [201]: Systems that run the business versus systems that analyze it.
- [Data Modeling Basics](01_foundations/Data%20Modeling%20Basics.md) [201]: Deciding which tables to have and how they connect, covering normalization, entities, and grain.
- [Star Schema](01_foundations/Star%20Schema.md) [201]: Fact and dimension tables, the classic shape for analytics.
- [Servers and the Cloud](01_foundations/Servers%20and%20the%20Cloud.md) [101]: Computers you rent by the minute from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google.
- [Storage vs Compute](01_foundations/Storage%20vs%20Compute.md) [101]: The split between where data sits and what crunches it, the most important idea in modern data.
- [Python for Data](01_foundations/Python%20for%20Data.md) [101]: Why Python and pandas became the default language for data work.
- [APIs](01_foundations/APIs.md) [101]: How software talks to other software, and how most SaaS data gets pulled out.
- [ETL vs ELT](01_foundations/ETL%20vs%20ELT.md) [101]: Extract, transform, load, and why the order flipped in the cloud.
- [Batch vs Streaming](01_foundations/Batch%20vs%20Streaming.md) [101]: Processing data in scheduled chunks versus continuously as it arrives.

## The Big Data Era

- [Chapter 02 - The Big Data Era](02_big_data_era/Chapter%2002%20-%20The%20Big%20Data%20Era.md): When data outgrew one computer, from Google's papers to Hadoop and the pain that came with it.
- [The Three Vs of Big Data](02_big_data_era/The%20Three%20Vs%20of%20Big%20Data.md) [101]: Volume, velocity, and variety, the three ways data got too big for one machine.
- [Scaling Up vs Scaling Out](02_big_data_era/Scaling%20Up%20vs%20Scaling%20Out.md) [101]: Buying a bigger computer versus using many small ones.
- [Distributed Systems](02_big_data_era/Distributed%20Systems.md) [201]: Many computers acting as one, and the new failure modes that come with it.
- [Google File System and MapReduce Papers](02_big_data_era/Google%20File%20System%20and%20MapReduce%20Papers.md) [201]: The 2003 and 2004 Google papers that started the big data era.
- [Apache Hadoop](02_big_data_era/Apache%20Hadoop.md) [101]: The open-source system that let ordinary companies store and process huge data on cheap machines.
- [HDFS](02_big_data_era/HDFS.md) [201]: Hadoop's distributed file system, which splits files into replicated blocks across many machines.
- [MapReduce](02_big_data_era/MapReduce.md) [201]: Hadoop's map-then-reduce processing model, which was powerful, slow, and painful to write.
- [YARN](02_big_data_era/YARN.md) [301]: Hadoop's resource manager, which decides which job gets which machines.
- [Apache Hive](02_big_data_era/Apache%20Hive.md) [201]: SQL on Hadoop, which made big data queryable by analysts.
- [Hive Metastore](02_big_data_era/Hive%20Metastore.md) [201]: The table directory Hive introduced, which Spark and early Databricks inherited.
- [Apache HBase](02_big_data_era/Apache%20HBase.md) [301]: A fast key-value database on top of HDFS, modeled after Google Bigtable.
- [Cloudera and Hortonworks](02_big_data_era/Cloudera%20and%20Hortonworks.md) [201]: The companies that sold supported Hadoop, and why they merged in 2019.
- [Columnar Storage](02_big_data_era/Columnar%20Storage.md) [201]: Storing data column by column so analytics reads only what it needs.
- [Apache Parquet](02_big_data_era/Apache%20Parquet.md) [201]: The open columnar file format underneath Delta Lake, Iceberg, and most of the lakehouse.
- [Apache ORC](02_big_data_era/Apache%20ORC.md) [301]: Hive's columnar format, Parquet's sibling and rival.
- [The Pain of Hadoop](02_big_data_era/The%20Pain%20of%20Hadoop.md) [101]: Why Hadoop clusters became slow, expensive, and hard to staff, which set the stage for Spark and the cloud.

## Apache Spark

- [Chapter 03 - Apache Spark](03_apache_spark/Chapter%2003%20-%20Apache%20Spark.md): The faster, friendlier engine born at UC Berkeley that replaced MapReduce and became Databricks' foundation.
- [AMPLab and the Birth of Spark](03_apache_spark/AMPLab%20and%20the%20Birth%20of%20Spark.md) [101]: How a Berkeley research lab built Spark in 2009, and how its creators went on to found Databricks.
- [Apache Spark](03_apache_spark/Apache%20Spark.md) [101]: The open-source engine for processing big data in memory across a cluster.
- [RDDs](03_apache_spark/RDDs.md) [301]: Resilient distributed datasets, Spark's original low-level building block.
- [Lazy Evaluation](03_apache_spark/Lazy%20Evaluation.md) [201]: Why Spark plans the whole job before running any of it.
- [Transformations and Actions](03_apache_spark/Transformations%20and%20Actions.md) [201]: The two kinds of Spark operations, ones that describe work and ones that trigger it.
- [DataFrames](03_apache_spark/DataFrames.md) [101]: Tables in code, with named columns and types, the main way people use Spark today.
- [Spark SQL](03_apache_spark/Spark%20SQL.md) [101]: Running SQL on Spark, the bridge from Hive to Databricks SQL.
- [Catalyst Optimizer](03_apache_spark/Catalyst%20Optimizer.md) [301]: The query planner that rewrites your SQL and DataFrame code into a faster plan.
- [Tungsten](03_apache_spark/Tungsten.md) [401]: Spark's memory-management and code-generation engine work, the precursor to Photon.
- [Driver and Executors](03_apache_spark/Driver%20and%20Executors.md) [201]: The boss process and the worker processes in every Spark cluster.
- [Partitions](03_apache_spark/Partitions.md) [201]: How Spark slices data so many machines can work on it at once.
- [Shuffles](03_apache_spark/Shuffles.md) [301]: Moving data between machines, the most expensive thing Spark does.
- [Jobs Stages and Tasks](03_apache_spark/Jobs%20Stages%20and%20Tasks.md) [301]: How Spark breaks one query into jobs, stages, and tasks you can see in the Spark UI.
- [PySpark](03_apache_spark/PySpark.md) [101]: Spark from Python, the interface most data teams use.
- [Structured Streaming](03_apache_spark/Structured%20Streaming.md) [201]: Spark's engine for treating a live stream like a table that keeps growing.
- [MLlib](03_apache_spark/MLlib.md) [201]: Spark's built-in library for distributed machine learning on DataFrames.
- [Adaptive Query Execution](03_apache_spark/Adaptive%20Query%20Execution.md) [301]: Spark re-planning a query during execution based on runtime statistics.
- [Spark Connect](03_apache_spark/Spark%20Connect.md) [301]: The client-server protocol that lets thin clients run Spark DataFrame code on a remote Spark server.
- [Spark UI](03_apache_spark/Spark%20UI.md) [201]: The built-in web interface for seeing what a Spark application did and why it was slow.
- [Pandas API on Spark](03_apache_spark/Pandas%20API%20on%20Spark.md) [201]: Running pandas-style code on Spark for data too large for one machine.

## The Modern Data Stack

- [Chapter 04 - The Modern Data Stack](04_modern_data_stack/Chapter%2004%20-%20The%20Modern%20Data%20Stack.md): Cloud warehouses, data lakes, Kafka, Airflow, and dbt, and the messy two-tier world they created.
- [Data Warehouses](04_modern_data_stack/Data%20Warehouses.md) [101]: A database built for analytics, which is clean, fast, and expensive.
- [Amazon Redshift](04_modern_data_stack/Amazon%20Redshift.md) [201]: AWS's cloud data warehouse, previewed in 2012 and generally available in 2013.
- [Snowflake](04_modern_data_stack/Snowflake.md) [201]: The cloud warehouse that separated storage and compute, and Databricks' best-known rival.
- [Google BigQuery](04_modern_data_stack/Google%20BigQuery.md) [201]: Google's serverless warehouse, where you run SQL without sizing or managing any servers.
- [Data Lakes](04_modern_data_stack/Data%20Lakes.md) [101]: Dumping every file into cheap storage first and figuring it out later.
- [Object Storage](04_modern_data_stack/Object%20Storage.md) [101]: Cheap, effectively unlimited cloud file storage, which is the floor the lakehouse stands on.
- [Amazon S3](04_modern_data_stack/Amazon%20S3.md) [101]: AWS object storage, launched in 2006, the original cloud data lake.
- [Azure Data Lake Storage](04_modern_data_stack/Azure%20Data%20Lake%20Storage.md) [101]: Azure's object storage built for analytics, Blob Storage with a hierarchical namespace (formerly ADLS Gen2).
- [Google Cloud Storage](04_modern_data_stack/Google%20Cloud%20Storage.md) [101]: Google Cloud's object storage, addressed as gs://bucket/path.
- [Data Swamps](04_modern_data_stack/Data%20Swamps.md) [101]: What a data lake becomes without rules, with no trust, no quality, and no one knowing what is where.
- [Apache Kafka](04_modern_data_stack/Apache%20Kafka.md) [201]: The event-streaming backbone that moves live data between systems.
- [Apache Airflow](04_modern_data_stack/Apache%20Airflow.md) [201]: The open-source scheduler that runs pipelines as DAGs written in Python.
- [dbt](04_modern_data_stack/dbt.md) [201]: SQL transformations with software engineering habits like version control and tests.
- [Fivetran and ELT Tools](04_modern_data_stack/Fivetran%20and%20ELT%20Tools.md) [201]: Managed connectors that copy SaaS and database data into a warehouse or lakehouse.
- [BI Tools](04_modern_data_stack/BI%20Tools.md) [101]: Power BI, Tableau, Looker, and similar tools that turn tables into dashboards and reports.
- [The Two-Tier Architecture Problem](04_modern_data_stack/The%20Two-Tier%20Architecture%20Problem.md) [101]: Running a lake and a warehouse side by side means two copies, two bills, stale data, and no AI on warehouse data.

## The Lakehouse

- [Chapter 05 - The Lakehouse](05_lakehouse/Chapter%2005%20-%20The%20Lakehouse.md): Warehouse reliability on lake storage, through Delta Lake, open table formats, and the medallion architecture.
- [The Lakehouse Idea](05_lakehouse/The%20Lakehouse%20Idea.md) [101]: One copy of data in open files on cheap storage, with warehouse-grade reliability and speed.
- [The Lakehouse Paper](05_lakehouse/The%20Lakehouse%20Paper.md) [301]: The 2021 CIDR paper that named and argued for the lakehouse.
- [ACID Transactions](05_lakehouse/ACID%20Transactions.md) [201]: The four guarantees that stop half-written, conflicting, or lost data.
- [Open Table Formats](05_lakehouse/Open%20Table%20Formats.md) [201]: A metadata layer over Parquet files that turns a folder into a real table.
- [Delta Lake](05_lakehouse/Delta%20Lake.md) [101]: Databricks' open-source table format and the default for every table on the platform.
- [Delta Transaction Log](05_lakehouse/Delta%20Transaction%20Log.md) [301]: The _delta_log folder of JSON commits that makes Delta Lake transactional.
- [Time Travel](05_lakehouse/Time%20Travel.md) [201]: Querying a table as it was yesterday, and undoing mistakes.
- [Schema Enforcement and Evolution](05_lakehouse/Schema%20Enforcement%20and%20Evolution.md) [201]: Rejecting bad columns, and safely adding new ones.
- [MERGE and Upserts](05_lakehouse/MERGE%20and%20Upserts.md) [201]: Insert-or-update in one statement, the workhorse of incremental pipelines.
- [Apache Iceberg](05_lakehouse/Apache%20Iceberg.md) [201]: The Netflix-born table format, Delta's main rival, now first-class in Unity Catalog.
- [Apache Hudi](05_lakehouse/Apache%20Hudi.md) [301]: The Uber-born table format focused on upserts and incremental processing.
- [Delta UniForm](05_lakehouse/Delta%20UniForm.md) [301]: Writing Delta tables that Iceberg readers can also read.
- [Medallion Architecture](05_lakehouse/Medallion%20Architecture.md) [101]: Bronze (raw), silver (cleaned), and gold (business-ready) layers of tables.
- [Liquid Clustering](05_lakehouse/Liquid%20Clustering.md) [301]: Self-organizing data layout that replaced partitioning and Z-ordering for most tables.
- [Deletion Vectors](05_lakehouse/Deletion%20Vectors.md) [401]: Marking rows deleted instead of rewriting whole files.
- [Change Data Feed](05_lakehouse/Change%20Data%20Feed.md) [301]: A row-level log of what changed in a Delta table, for downstream incremental processing.
- [OPTIMIZE and VACUUM](05_lakehouse/OPTIMIZE%20and%20VACUUM.md) [301]: Compacting small files and deleting old ones, and Predictive Optimization doing it for you.
- [Predictive Optimization](05_lakehouse/Predictive%20Optimization.md) [201]: Databricks automatically running OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, and statistics collection on Unity Catalog managed tables.

## Databricks Platform

- [Chapter 06 - The Databricks Platform](06_databricks_platform/Chapter%2006%20-%20The%20Databricks%20Platform.md): Databricks arrives. Accounts, workspaces, compute, notebooks, and the tools for building on it.
- [The Founding of Databricks](06_databricks_platform/The%20Founding%20of%20Databricks.md) [101]: How Spark's creators started a company in 2013 to run Spark in the cloud.
- [The Data Intelligence Platform](06_databricks_platform/The%20Data%20Intelligence%20Platform.md) [101]: Databricks' name for the lakehouse plus AI that understands your data (now often called the Data + AI Platform).
- [Accounts and Workspaces](06_databricks_platform/Accounts%20and%20Workspaces.md) [101]: The account is the company, and a workspace is a room where teams work.
- [Control Plane and Compute Plane](06_databricks_platform/Control%20Plane%20and%20Compute%20Plane.md) [201]: What Databricks runs for you, versus what runs in your cloud account or in serverless.
- [Databricks Runtime](06_databricks_platform/Databricks%20Runtime.md) [201]: The tuned Spark plus libraries image every classic cluster boots, and its LTS versions.
- [Photon](06_databricks_platform/Photon.md) [301]: Databricks' C++ query engine that speeds up SQL and DataFrame work.
- [Compute Types](06_databricks_platform/Compute%20Types.md) [101]: The map of Databricks compute, covering all-purpose, jobs, serverless, and SQL warehouses.
- [All-Purpose Compute](06_databricks_platform/All-Purpose%20Compute.md) [201]: Interactive clusters for notebooks and exploration, which you create, share, and must remember to stop.
- [Jobs Compute](06_databricks_platform/Jobs%20Compute.md) [201]: Clusters that spin up for one scheduled job and then disappear, at a lower price.
- [Serverless Compute](06_databricks_platform/Serverless%20Compute.md) [101]: Compute that Databricks runs and scales for you, starting in seconds with no clusters to configure.
- [SQL Warehouses](06_databricks_platform/SQL%20Warehouses.md) [101]: Compute built for SQL queries, dashboards, and BI tools, in serverless, pro, and classic types.
- [Notebooks](06_databricks_platform/Notebooks.md) [101]: Web documents that mix runnable code cells in Python, SQL, Scala, or R with results, charts, and text.
- [Genie Code](06_databricks_platform/Genie%20Code.md) [101]: The built-in AI coding and data agent, renamed from Databricks Assistant to Genie Code in March 2026.
- [Git Folders and Workspace Files](06_databricks_platform/Git%20Folders%20and%20Workspace%20Files.md) [201]: Git folders sync workspace code with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, or CodeCommit; workspace files store code beside notebooks.
- [Declarative Automation Bundles](06_databricks_platform/Declarative%20Automation%20Bundles.md) [301]: Infrastructure as code for jobs, pipelines, and apps, defined as YAML in Git and deployed with `databricks bundle` (formerly Databricks Asset Bundles).
- [Databricks CLI](06_databricks_platform/Databricks%20CLI.md) [201]: The `databricks` command-line tool for scripting workspaces and accounts, authenticating, and deploying bundles.
- [Databricks SDKs and REST API](06_databricks_platform/Databricks%20SDKs%20and%20REST%20API.md) [301]: Programmatic control of Databricks through the REST API and the official SDKs for Python, Java, Go, and JavaScript (plus an R SDK from Databricks Labs).
- [Databricks Connect](06_databricks_platform/Databricks%20Connect.md) [301]: A client library, built on Spark Connect, that runs Spark code from your local IDE on Databricks clusters or serverless compute.
- [DBUs](06_databricks_platform/DBUs.md) [101]: The Databricks Unit (DBU), a normalized unit of processing power per hour that Databricks usage is measured and priced in.
- [Libraries and Environments](06_databricks_platform/Libraries%20and%20Environments.md) [201]: How to install Python, JAR, and R packages and pin dependencies with notebook-scoped libraries, compute-scoped libraries, and serverless environments.
- [Serverless Workspaces and Default Storage](06_databricks_platform/Serverless%20Workspaces%20and%20Default%20Storage.md) [201]: Workspaces that run only on serverless compute and store data in Databricks-managed storage, with no cloud setup.
- [dbutils and Widgets](06_databricks_platform/dbutils%20and%20Widgets.md) [201]: The notebook utility library for files, secrets, and job values, and widgets for notebook parameters.
- [Instance Pools](06_databricks_platform/Instance%20Pools.md) [301]: Pre-warmed idle VMs that cut classic cluster start time.
- [Init Scripts](06_databricks_platform/Init%20Scripts.md) [301]: Shell scripts that run on each classic cluster node at startup, and where to store them safely.
- [DBFS](06_databricks_platform/DBFS.md) [201]: The legacy Databricks File System and mounts, and why Unity Catalog volumes replace them.

## Unity Catalog & Governance

- [Chapter 07 - Unity Catalog and Governance](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Chapter%2007%20-%20Unity%20Catalog%20and%20Governance.md): One place to find, secure, track, and share every data and AI asset.
- [Unity Catalog](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Unity%20Catalog.md) [101]: Databricks' governance layer for permissions, discovery, lineage, and auditing across every workspace.
- [Metastore](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Metastore.md) [201]: The top-level Unity Catalog container, one per region, that holds every catalog, credential, share, and connection.
- [Three-Level Namespace](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Three-Level%20Namespace.md) [101]: catalog.schema.table, the three-part address of every table, view, volume, function, and model.
- [Catalogs Schemas and Tables](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Catalogs%20Schemas%20and%20Tables.md) [101]: The securable objects in Unity Catalog (catalogs, schemas, tables, views, volumes, functions, models) and how to organize them.
- [Managed vs External Tables](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Managed%20vs%20External%20Tables.md) [201]: Who owns the files, and what happens when you drop a table. Managed is the default and recommended choice.
- [Volumes](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Volumes.md) [201]: Governed folders for non-table files like CSVs, images, PDFs, and model artifacts, addressed as /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume.
- [Storage Credentials and External Locations](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Storage%20Credentials%20and%20External%20Locations.md) [301]: How Unity Catalog is allowed to reach your cloud storage, with credentials held by the catalog instead of by clusters.
- [Privileges and Grants](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Privileges%20and%20Grants.md) [201]: GRANT and REVOKE on securable objects, how privileges inherit down the tree, and how ownership and MANAGE work.
- [Row Filters and Column Masks](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Row%20Filters%20and%20Column%20Masks.md) [301]: SQL functions attached to a table that show each person only the rows and column values they are allowed to see.
- [Attribute-Based Access Control](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Attribute-Based%20Access%20Control.md) [301]: Policies driven by governed tags, set once on a catalog or schema, that filter rows and mask columns on every matching table.
- [Data Lineage](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Data%20Lineage.md) [201]: An automatic, column-level map of where every table and column came from and where it goes, captured by Unity Catalog at runtime.
- [Audit Logs](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Audit%20Logs.md) [301]: A record of who did what and when across the account, queryable as system.access.audit or delivered to your own storage.
- [System Tables](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/System%20Tables.md) [201]: Databricks' own operational data (billing, audit, lineage, compute, jobs, queries) as queryable tables in the system catalog.
- [Lakehouse Federation](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Lakehouse%20Federation.md) [201]: Querying Postgres, SQL Server, Snowflake, BigQuery, and other databases and catalogs in place through Unity Catalog, without copying.
- [OpenSharing](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/OpenSharing.md) [201]: The open protocol, formerly Delta Sharing, for sharing live data and AI assets with anyone, on Databricks or not, without copying.
- [Clean Rooms](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Clean%20Rooms.md) [301]: A governed, serverless environment where up to ten organizations run approved analysis on combined data without seeing each other's raw records.
- [Databricks Marketplace](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Databricks%20Marketplace.md) [201]: An open marketplace for finding and getting datasets, ML models, and other data products from providers, delivered through OpenSharing.
- [Data Classification](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Data%20Classification.md) [301]: A Unity Catalog feature that scans catalogs for sensitive data such as PII and can tag matching columns automatically.
- [Hive Metastore Migration to Unity Catalog](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Hive%20Metastore%20Migration%20to%20Unity%20Catalog.md) [301]: Upgrading older workspaces from the legacy Hive metastore to Unity Catalog with federation, SYNC, CLONE, and the UCX utilities.
- [Catalog Explorer](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Catalog%20Explorer.md) [101]: The Unity Catalog UI for browsing, searching, and managing data and AI assets and their permissions.
- [Governed Tags](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Governed%20Tags.md) [201]: Account-level tag definitions with controlled values, used for discovery, classification, and ABAC policies.
- [Service Credentials](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Service%20Credentials.md) [301]: Unity Catalog objects that let code reach cloud services other than storage, such as queues or secret stores.
- [Unity Catalog Functions](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Unity%20Catalog%20Functions.md) [201]: SQL and Python functions registered in Unity Catalog, governed and reusable across queries, agents, and tools.
- [Lakeguard](07_unity_catalog_and_governance/Lakeguard.md) [301]: The isolation technology that lets many users share standard and serverless compute while Unity Catalog enforces fine-grained access.

## Data Engineering

- [Chapter 08 - Data Engineering](08_data_engineering/Chapter%2008%20-%20Data%20Engineering.md): Getting data in, cleaning it, and running it on schedule with Lakeflow.

- [Lakeflow Connect](08_data_engineering/Lakeflow%20Connect.md) [101]: Managed connectors for Salesforce, SQL Server, Google Analytics, and other common sources.

- [Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines](08_data_engineering/Lakeflow%20Spark%20Declarative%20Pipelines.md) [201]: Declaring the tables you want and letting Databricks run, retry, and track the pipeline (formerly Delta Live Tables).
- [Streaming Tables](08_data_engineering/Streaming%20Tables.md) [201]: Tables that keep themselves up to date from a stream or growing source.
- [Materialized Views](08_data_engineering/Materialized%20Views.md) [201]: Precomputed query results that refresh incrementally.
- [Expectations and Data Quality](08_data_engineering/Expectations%20and%20Data%20Quality.md) [201]: Rules on your data that warn, drop, or stop the pipeline when broken.
- [Change Data Capture](08_data_engineering/Change%20Data%20Capture.md) [301]: Copying only what changed in a source database, with AUTO CDC.
- [Slowly Changing Dimensions](08_data_engineering/Slowly%20Changing%20Dimensions.md) [301]: SCD type 1 and type 2, which decide whether to keep history when a customer moves.
- [Lakeflow Jobs](08_data_engineering/Lakeflow%20Jobs.md) [101]: Databricks' built-in orchestrator for scheduled multi-task workflows (formerly Workflows).
- [Tasks Triggers and Schedules](08_data_engineering/Tasks%20Triggers%20and%20Schedules.md) [201]: Task types, dependencies, file-arrival and table-update triggers, and retries.
- [Lakeflow Designer](08_data_engineering/Lakeflow%20Designer.md) [101]: A no-code, drag-and-drop pipeline builder with AI help.
- [Structured Streaming on Databricks](08_data_engineering/Structured%20Streaming%20on%20Databricks.md) [301]: Running Spark streams on Databricks, covering Kafka sources, checkpoints, and real-time mode.
- [dbt on Databricks](08_data_engineering/dbt%20on%20Databricks.md) [201]: Running dbt projects against Databricks SQL, and as job tasks.
- [CI-CD for Data Pipelines](08_data_engineering/CI-CD%20for%20Data%20Pipelines.md) [301]: Dev, staging, and prod, with tests and automated deployment for data code.
- [Testing Data Pipelines](08_data_engineering/Testing%20Data%20Pipelines.md) [301]: Unit tests, data tests, and expectations for code that moves data.

- [MosaicML and Open Models](10_ai_and_ml/MosaicML%20and%20Open%20Models.md) [201]: Databricks' 2023 MosaicML acquisition, the MPT and DBRX open models, and how that technology lives on in hosted models, serving, and AI Runtime.

## Migrating to Databricks

- [Chapter 15 - Migrating to Databricks](15_migrating_to_databricks/Chapter%2015%20-%20Migrating%20to%20Databricks.md): Playbooks for moving a business onto Databricks from spreadsheets, databases, warehouses, and Hadoop.
- [Migration Strategy Overview](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migration%20Strategy%20Overview.md) [101]: The phases of every migration, from assess and plan to coexist, ingest, convert, validate, switch over, and decommission.
- [Assessing Your Current Data Estate](15_migrating_to_databricks/Assessing%20Your%20Current%20Data%20Estate.md) [201]: Taking inventory of sources, tables, jobs, reports, users, and costs before moving anything.
- [Migrating from Excel and Access](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Excel%20and%20Access.md) [101]: Moving a spreadsheet-run business into governed tables, with file uploads, Volumes, a first dashboard, and Genie Agents.
- [Migrating from SQL Server](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20SQL%20Server.md) [201]: Moving off an on-premises or Azure SQL Server, using federation first, Lakeflow Connect replication after, and Lakebridge for T-SQL.
- [Migrating from Postgres and MySQL](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Postgres%20and%20MySQL.md) [201]: Moving app-database analytics from PostgreSQL or MySQL into the lakehouse without slowing the app down.
- [Migrating from Snowflake](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Snowflake.md) [301]: A Snowflake-to-Databricks playbook covering federation, Iceberg-based coexistence, data unloads, SQL conversion with Lakebridge, and reconciliation.
- [Migrating from Amazon Redshift](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Amazon%20Redshift.md) [301]: A Redshift-to-Databricks playbook covering federation, UNLOAD to S3 as Parquet, SQL conversion with Lakebridge, and switch-over.
- [Migrating from Google BigQuery](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Google%20BigQuery.md) [301]: A BigQuery-to-Databricks playbook covering Storage API federation, EXPORT DATA to Cloud Storage, SQL conversion, and reconciliation.
- [Migrating from Hadoop](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20from%20Hadoop.md) [301]: Moving HDFS data, Hive tables, Spark jobs, and Oozie workflows off an on-premises Hadoop cluster into Databricks.
- [Migrating ETL Tools](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20ETL%20Tools.md) [301]: Converting SSIS, DataStage, Informatica, Talend, Airflow, and stored procedures into Databricks notebooks, SQL, pipelines, and jobs.
- [Lakebridge](15_migrating_to_databricks/Lakebridge.md) [301]: Databricks' free migration toolkit for profiling, SQL conversion, and data reconciliation.
- [Migrating BI Reports](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migrating%20BI%20Reports.md) [201]: Repointing Power BI and Tableau reports to Databricks SQL warehouses, or rebuilding them as AI/BI dashboards and Genie agents.
- [Running Old and New in Parallel](15_migrating_to_databricks/Running%20Old%20and%20New%20in%20Parallel.md) [201]: Parallel runs, reconciliation with Lakebridge and SQL, and a safe switch-over and rollback plan.
- [Migration Checklist](15_migrating_to_databricks/Migration%20Checklist.md) [101]: A printable, start-to-finish checklist for a small business migration.

## Learning Paths

- [Chapter 80 - Learning Paths](80_learning_paths/Chapter%2080%20-%20Learning%20Paths.md): Curated routes through the graph for each kind of reader, from total beginner to expert.
- [Path - Absolute Beginner](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Absolute%20Beginner.md) [101]: Zero to "I get what Databricks is" in about 20 notes.
- [Path - Business Owner](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Business%20Owner.md) [101]: Everything a decision-maker needs, covering fit, cost, risk, and the first 30 days.
- [Path - Analyst](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Analyst.md) [101]: From Excel and SQL to Databricks SQL, dashboards, Genie Agents, and Power BI.
- [Path - Data Engineer](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Data%20Engineer.md) [201]: Ingestion, the lakehouse, pipelines, orchestration, and CI/CD.
- [Path - Data Scientist and ML Engineer](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Data%20Scientist%20and%20ML%20Engineer.md) [201]: Notebooks, Spark, MLflow, the feature store, and serving.
- [Path - AI App Developer](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20AI%20App%20Developer.md) [201]: LLMs, RAG, AI Search, agents, Databricks Apps, and Lakebase.
- [Path - Platform Admin](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Platform%20Admin.md) [301]: Accounts, identity, Unity Catalog, networking, and cost controls on your cloud.
- [Path - One-Person Data Team](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20One-Person%20Data%20Team.md) [101]: The shortest route for a small business with one data person doing every job.
- [Path - Azure Deep Dive](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Azure%20Deep%20Dive.md) [301]: Every Azure-specific rabbit hole in order.
- [Path - AWS Deep Dive](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20AWS%20Deep%20Dive.md) [301]: Every AWS-specific rabbit hole in order.
- [Path - Google Cloud Deep Dive](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Google%20Cloud%20Deep%20Dive.md) [301]: Every Google Cloud-specific rabbit hole in order.
- [Path - Certification Prep](80_learning_paths/Path%20-%20Certification%20Prep.md) [301]: Which Databricks certifications exist and which notes map to each exam.
